Subject: Suspicious promo-credit requests from quicktests.io

Team — flagging a cluster of promo-credit requests that look automated. Summary: 6 signups over ~90 minutes, all from the quicktests.io domain (ops@quicktests.io, qa@quicktests.io variants), very similar display names (e.g., QA Ops 1, QA Ops-2), and three accounts already received the automatic onboarding credits this morning via self-serve. IPs resolve to a /22 in us-west, reverse lookup shows a generic cloud provider.

I'm attaching a CSV with the signup rows and a short IP lookup. Can we pause any further self-serve credit issuance for that domain and check whether these map to a single organization or are throwaway addresses?

Immediate asks: 
- Dev: can you confirm whether these accounts have overlapping device/KV cache signatures?
- Mina: can security put a 24h hold on promo issuance for this domain if we think it's abuse?
- Neha/Marissa: any commercial relationship here? I couldn't find a legit HubSpot company record, only a scraped listing.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Adding more context — I dug into the HubSpot link and found a very thin company record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/98765 (no traffic data, no billing contact). I also confirmed one credit issuance this morning: user qa.ops1@quicktests.io was granted $50 in self-serve credits at 08:14 PST. I've attached the issued credits report slice.

Full headers for qa.ops1@quicktests.io (redacted for thread):
- Received: from 52.14.122.XXX (unknown)
- SPF: pass
- DKIM: none

Notably: email domain uses generic mail routing (no corporate MTA), and DMARC is relaxed. The pattern looks like a scripted signup using cloud VMs.

I agree we should reverse the $50 if we classify as abuse. I'm holding on further outreach until we have security's recommendation.

Good notes — I'm taking this on. Initial triage results: 
- Device/IP correlation from Dev shows 5 of the 6 signups share identical KV cache fingerprints and overlap on three fingerprint heuristics (user-agent string fuzz, session timing).
- ASN lookup ties the IPs to a large cloud hosting provider commonly used for automated testing.

Action plan (SUP-3427 created):
1) Place a 24-hour hold on any automatic promo credit issuance for quicktests.io and related subdomains.
2) Reverse the $50 credit to qa.ops1@quicktests.io pending verification (we'll note the reversal in billing).
3) Rafael: please send a verification request to the contact asking for corporate registration or a business domain proof; ask them to reply to this thread and attach a company URL or signed statement.
4) If we receive evasive responses or more signups appear, we'll escalate and implement an ASN block and expand rules in the promo guardrail.

I've opened SUP-3427 in Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3427 
I'll follow up with an update once reversals are processed.

--
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Hi — I'm Rafael from Redwood Inference, following up about the signups from @quicktests.io that requested promotional credits. To proceed we need quick verification so we can avoid delaying legitimate evaluations. Please reply with ONE of the following within 48 hours: 

1) A link to your corporate website that matches quicktests.io and a corporate contact (name + job title).
2) A short screenshot of a company admin page or an official invoice/registration document showing QuickTests Inc.
3) If you're evaluating via an internal testing team and not a registered company, please confirm that and provide a short sentence describing the evaluation use case and the number of seats/tests you intend to run.

Note: we've temporarily put a 24-hour hold on further automatic promo credits for quicktests.io while we validate. If we don't get a verifiable response within 48 hours we'll reverse any issued credits and mark the accounts as suspicious.

Thanks — Rafael
